exposure: maternal and infant plasma alpha-, gamma-, and delta-tocopherol levels
cohort: 189 mother-infant pairs from the Midwestern United States and 99 mother-infant pairs from Central Nigeria
finding: Increased circulating gamma-tocopherol was associated with negative outcomes like Caesarian sections, while increased alpha:gamma-tocopherol ratios were associated with positive outcomes such as vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Increased circulating gamma-tocopherol was associated with Caesarian sections, while increased alpha:gamma-tocopherol ratios were associated with vaginal delivery.
